open_points.subject: personal-data boundary for direct service access
open_points.text: “values of class `personal_data` (K-14) reach an agent only as digest and class” conflicts with “An agent's own access to a service ... is granted by that service and the owner outside the kernel” and “its personal-data promise (K-14) covers what the kernel itself returns.”
open_points.question: Is the claim that an agent receives personal data only as digest and class limited to values returned through the kernel, or must direct service access enforce it too?
options: Limit the claim to the kernel surface
Require services to apply the same disclosure rule to direct agent access
Prohibit direct agent access to personal data
open_points.default_guess: Limit the claim to the kernel surface.

open_points.subject: agent-written code outside the sandbox
open_points.text: “Agent-written code — untrusted forever; runs only inside the sandbox” conflicts with “the agent processes a photo itself, outside the kernel, with its own access to the service that holds the photo.”
open_points.question: Does “agent-written code” mean only code submitted as a kernel function, or is outside-the-kernel photo processing also required to run in a sandbox?
options: The sandbox rule covers only submitted kernel functions
All code written or invoked by an agent must be sandboxed
The direct photo-processing path is a specific exception
open_points.default_guess: Treat the sandbox rule as applying only to submitted kernel functions.

open_points.subject: owner authentication
open_points.text: “Reaches the kernel through the agent channel with the owner's token” names no source, validation rule, rotation rule or revocation rule for the owner's token; K-15 defines those matters only for agent tokens.
open_points.question: How is the owner token provisioned, validated, rotated and revoked, and how is it distinguished from an agent token?
options: A separately configured single owner token
An external identity assertion accepted from the reverse proxy
An agent token carrying an owner role
open_points.default_guess: Use a separately configured owner token, validated like agent tokens and reloadable after configuration changes.

open_points.subject: platform manifest trust boundary
open_points.text: “Microservices — known only as records of the platform manifest” and “the platform manifest and the repositories alone” do not identify who supplies the manifest, who may change it, or how the kernel authenticates the version it reads.
open_points.question: What is the trusted source of the platform manifest, and what makes a manifest record authoritative to the kernel?
options: A local installation-controlled file
A signed manifest fetched from a platform service
A named repository revision loaded operationally
open_points.default_guess: Treat an installation-controlled local manifest as trusted configuration.

open_points.subject: invalid microservice response
open_points.text: “their answers are untrusted data until validated at the port” does not say what observable result follows when an answer fails schema, media-type or disclosure validation.
open_points.question: What node, run and trace outcome results when a service answer fails validation, and may any part of that answer be retained or returned?
options: Fail the node and its dependants, record only bounded diagnostic metadata
Refuse the invocation as if it had not run
Rest the run for owner resolution
open_points.default_guess: Fail the node, stop its dependants, and retain only bounded non-secret diagnostics.

open_points.subject: echoed-secret response handling
open_points.text: “A service's own answer body that echoes one verbatim is withheld from everyone, the owner included, and never used as an output” does not state the resulting node status, run status, trace content or caller-visible reason.
open_points.question: What observable failure occurs when an answer body contains a configured secret verbatim?
options: Fail the node with a secret-detected reason
Treat the invocation as an unknown outcome
Succeed while replacing the output with a withheld marker
open_points.default_guess: Fail the node with a non-secret diagnostic and record only the response digest.

open_points.subject: secret-recognition set and comparison
open_points.text: “echoes one verbatim” does not define which configured secret values are checked, against which response representations, or whether matching is byte-exact after transport decoding.
open_points.question: Precisely which protected values and response bytes participate in verbatim secret detection?
options: Check every configured credential and token against the decoded body bytes
Check only the credential used for that service request
Check selected secret-bearing response fields
open_points.default_guess: Check all configured secret values against the decoded response-body bytes using exact byte matching.

open_points.subject: contract-version lifecycle
open_points.text: “the first contract of a new slot name creates the slot” and references to “the slot's current contract version” do not say how a later contract version becomes current or what happens to the previous activation.
open_points.question: When a new contract version is authored, does it automatically become the slot's current contract version, and does that immediately remove or preserve the old implementation activation?
options: Make the new contract version current with no active implementation
Require an explicit contract-version activation action
Keep the old contract version current until an implementation of the new version is admitted
open_points.default_guess: Make the new contract version current and leave it without an active implementation until admission succeeds.

open_points.subject: trial-case pass criterion
open_points.text: “trial evidence per case,” “the whole active corpus,” and “a failed real execution can be captured into it, so a repaired slot stays repaired” never define what a trial case contains or what it means for an implementation to pass a captured failure.
open_points.question: Does a trial case assert an exact expected output, only successful contract-conforming execution, an expected failure class, or another predicate, and how is that predicate obtained when a failed execution is captured?
options: Exact input and expected output
Input plus a requirement to complete successfully within the contract
Input plus an explicitly authored expected predicate
open_points.default_guess: Use the captured input with a requirement for successful contract-conforming execution; manually added cases may also carry an exact expected output.

open_points.subject: corpus growth versus current activation
open_points.text: “Each contract version has a trial corpus,” “Admission is a deterministic verdict over the whole active corpus,” and rollback requires an implementation “admitted over the current corpus,” but no text says what adding or capturing a case does to existing verdicts and the active implementation.
open_points.question: When the corpus changes, are old admission verdicts invalidated, is the active implementation automatically re-tested, and what happens if it fails the enlarged corpus?
options: Re-test automatically and deactivate on failure
Invalidate verdicts and block new runs until an explicit re-admission
Allow the current activation to continue while requiring current-corpus admission only for future activations
open_points.default_guess: Invalidate prior verdicts, automatically re-test the active implementation, and deactivate it if it fails.

open_points.subject: Python sandbox version and library set
open_points.text: “Functions are written in Python only” and “the Python standard library only” do not identify the Python implementation/version or the exact permitted module set, although admission is said to be deterministic.
open_points.question: Which Python runtime version and standard-library module allowlist define the execution environment, and how are changes to that environment versioned?
options: One installation-pinned Python version with an explicit allowlist
Any supported host Python with dangerous modules blocked
A fixed packaged runtime whose digest is part of admission evidence
open_points.default_guess: Use a fixed packaged Python runtime and explicit module allowlist, with the runtime digest recorded in admission evidence.

open_points.subject: schema identity
open_points.text: “An edge is valid when both ports carry the same schema” does not identify the schema language, canonical form or equality rule.
open_points.question: What schema representation is supported, and does “same” mean byte identity, canonical structural equality or mutual assignability?
options: Canonical JSON Schema equality
Byte-identical stored schema documents
A kernel-defined closed schema algebra with structural equality
open_points.default_guess: Use a kernel-defined closed schema algebra and canonical structural equality.

open_points.subject: digest identity
open_points.text: Contracts, implementations, values, traces and manifest records are repeatedly identified “by digest,” but no digest algorithm or canonical byte representation is named.
open_points.question: Which digest algorithm and canonical encodings define equality and identity for code, schemas, values, files and manifest operation records?
options: One domain-separated SHA-256 scheme over canonical encodings
Raw-byte SHA-256 for every object
Installation-selectable digest algorithms
open_points.default_guess: Use domain-separated SHA-256 over a specified canonical encoding for each object type.

open_points.subject: map execution semantics
open_points.text: “a map of a node over a collection” does not define output ordering, concurrency, collection bounds, or what happens when one mapped item fails or waits.
open_points.question: How does a mapped node execute and aggregate item results, especially when an item fails, awaits approval or becomes pending?
options: Sequential ordered execution with fail-per-item and dependent aggregation rules
Bounded parallel execution preserving input order
Treat any item failure or wait as the state of the whole mapped node
open_points.default_guess: Use bounded parallel execution, preserve input order, and make any failed item fail the mapped node while retaining per-item traces.

open_points.subject: guard semantics
open_points.text: “a guard on a declared closed value” does not say what is compared, how branches are declared, whether a default branch exists, or what skipped branches contribute to outputs and traces.
open_points.question: What is the exact data model and runtime behavior of a guard?
options: Equality match against an enumerated closed-schema value with exhaustive branches
Boolean-only guard with true and false branches
Enumerated branches plus an optional default
open_points.default_guess: Require exhaustive equality branches over a declared finite value set and mark unchosen nodes skipped.

open_points.subject: operation effect-class authority
open_points.text: “Authority lives on operation nodes” lists effect classes, but K-03 says a binding gives only typed input and output ports and never states who assigns or accepts an operation's effect class.
open_points.question: Where is an operation node's effect class declared, who is authorized to set it, and what immutable record does a flow proof rely on?
options: The platform manifest declares it and the owner accepts it with the binding
The proposing agent assigns it and the owner accepts the binding
The owner assigns it separately when activating a flow
open_points.default_guess: Put the effect class in the manifest operation record and pin it through the owner-accepted binding.

open_points.subject: service-call outcome classification
open_points.text: “pending when a service is unreachable or an outcome unknown” does not define which HTTP, transport, timeout or validation results are definitely failed, unreachable, or outcome-unknown, especially for each effect class.
open_points.question: How are connection failures, timeouts, non-2xx responses, truncated responses and invalid responses classified for reads, draft writes and approval-gated effects?
options: Classify by whether request transmission could have occurred, with effectful ambiguity becoming outcome-unknown
Treat all transport failures as unreachable and all HTTP responses as definite
Let each binding declare the classification
open_points.default_guess: Use transport evidence: before-send failures are unreachable, ambiguous post-send failures of effects are outcome-unknown, and definite HTTP or validation failures fail the node.

open_points.subject: idempotency-key definition
open_points.text: “The kernel supplies the declared idempotency key” and “Idempotency keys, exact replay and outcome handling exist only on operation nodes” do not define the key's derivation, scope, persistence or whether a resend reuses it.
open_points.question: What uniquely determines an idempotency key, where is it placed in the request, how long is it retained, and is the same key reused after `not_applied` resolution?
options: Stable per effect attempt and reused for every resend of that attempt
New key for every approved send
Binding-declared key field with kernel-generated stable value
open_points.default_guess: Use a binding-declared request location and a kernel-generated key stable for the logical effect attempt, including resends.

open_points.subject: standing-grant lifecycle across activation changes
open_points.text: A grant is for “a node of a flow's active version,” while an effect runs without asking when “the owner granted that exact flow version a standing approval”; nothing says what happens to a grant when another version becomes active or the old version is activated again.
open_points.question: Does changing the active flow version revoke, suspend or preserve grants belonging to the previously active version, and can they become effective again after reactivation?
options: Revoke grants permanently when their version stops being active
Preserve but suspend them, allowing resurrection on reactivation
Preserve them as records but require a fresh grant after every activation
open_points.default_guess: Revoke active grants when their flow version ceases to be active.

open_points.subject: standing grants for draft-write nodes
open_points.text: The grant action says “the node of that flow version stops asking,” but `draft-write` nodes already run under flow activation and K-08 requires runtime approval only for `state-transition`, `external-effect` and `destructive`. Only `destructive` is expressly ineligible for a grant.
open_points.question: May a standing approval be granted to `read` or `draft-write` nodes, and if so, what observable behavior does such a grant change?
options: Only state-transition and external-effect nodes are grantable
Every non-destructive operation node is grantable even if the grant is operationally redundant
Draft-write nodes need grants despite the activation statement
open_points.default_guess: Allow grants only for state-transition and external-effect nodes.

open_points.subject: mixed waiting reasons
open_points.text: A run “rests `awaiting_approval`, or `pending` when a service is unreachable or an outcome unknown,” while resume retries unreachable nodes “whatever else the run waits for.”
open_points.question: What single observable run status and reason set is recorded when different nodes simultaneously await approval, wait for an unreachable service and wait on an unknown outcome?
options: One status plus a set of node-level waiting reasons
A precedence rule selecting one run status
Multiple simultaneous run statuses
open_points.default_guess: Store node-level waiting reasons and derive one run status by a specified precedence rule.

open_points.subject: trace records for retries and resumes
open_points.text: “Every node execution writes one immutable trace record” does not say whether retrying a node after resume appends another execution record or attempts to update the existing record.
open_points.question: How are multiple attempts of the same node execution represented while preserving immutable traces and effect-attempt history?
options: One immutable trace record per attempt linked to one logical node execution
One immutable record for the logical node plus separate immutable attempt records
A replacement record superseding the prior one
open_points.default_guess: Write one immutable trace per attempt, linked by run, node and logical execution identifier.

open_points.subject: cancellation during an in-flight service call
open_points.text: “the run ends `cancelled`; nothing further is sent” does not define what happens when cancellation races with a request already being transmitted or awaiting its response.
open_points.question: Can cancellation interrupt an in-flight call, and how are an already-sent effect and an ambiguous cancellation race recorded?
options: Do not interrupt an in-flight call; stop only later sends and record its eventual or unknown outcome
Abort the transport and classify an effect as outcome-unknown
Refuse cancellation while any call is in flight
open_points.default_guess: Stop future sends, abort when possible, and record an in-flight effect as outcome-unknown if its application cannot be determined.

open_points.subject: bounds for operation and flow values
open_points.text: The kernel stores “bounded values that edges carry” and traces contain “no unbounded payload,” but only function contracts are said to declare resource bounds.
open_points.question: Where are maximum sizes for flow inputs, operation responses, collections, trace fields and spooled files declared, and what failure occurs when one is exceeded?
options: Installation-wide bounds
Bounds declared by every port and binding
A combination of installation ceilings and narrower contract or binding bounds
open_points.default_guess: Use installation-wide ceilings with optional narrower per-port and per-binding bounds; exceeding one fails the node without retaining the oversized payload.

open_points.subject: rehearsing effectful flows
open_points.text: “Effectful flows are rehearsed on an installation of disposable rigs” promises an activity for which no actor, action, output or failure is defined.
open_points.question: Who starts a rehearsal, how it differs from an ordinary run, what evidence it produces, and whether successful rehearsal is required before production activation are all unspecified.
options: A normal run performed in a separately configured rig installation
A distinct rehearsal action that gates activation
An operational practice outside the kernel with no kernel-visible result
open_points.default_guess: Treat rehearsal as an ordinary run on a separately provisioned rig installation and do not make it a kernel gate.

open_points.subject: fixed MCP operation set versus primary actions
open_points.text: K-11 says the fixed operations are “inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel,” while Primary actions separately require capturing a failed execution, releasing a failed run, rolling back a slot, proposing a binding, composing and proving a flow, and refusing an effect.
open_points.question: Are those primary actions separate MCP operations, or which named K-11 operation carries each one and preserves its distinct authorization and result?
options: Add each missing primary action to the fixed MCP set
Define them as typed variants of `author`, `activate`, `approve` or `resolve`
Expose one generic command operation with tagged action variants
open_points.default_guess: Expose distinct typed MCP operations for capture, release, rollback, propose binding, compose/prove and refuse effect, and list them explicitly in K-11.
